text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: BUG_AUDIT_2026-09-13.md
+# Entire CLI bug audit — 2026-09-13
+
+Audited local HEAD `8a43e78f1`. Focus: setup persistence, import cancellation,
+session adoption, and transcript restoration. This is a bounded audit, not an
+exhaustive review of the repository. Findings are based on source, existing
+docs/tests, and isolated reproduction tests. The checkpoint payload requested
+for historical context was unavailable locally. Remote issue/PR ownership was
+not checked.
+
+## 1. P1 — Local setup erases the external-agent grant it just enabled
+
+Location: `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:1416`, with the earlier grant at line 1371.
+
+Trigger: first-time setup through the agent-selection flow, with `--local`,
+selecting an external agent. This includes the automatic selection used by
+`entire enable --local --yes` when an external agent is available.
+
+`runEnableInteractive` saves the initial settings struct, then
+`enableExternalAgentsLocally` writes and verifies `external_agents: true` in the
+local file. The telemetry step saves the original struct again. That struct
+still has `ExternalAgents == false`, and serialization omits the field, erasing
+the grant. Setup prints `Ready.`; a fresh settings load disables discovery of
+the plugin whose hooks were just installed.
+
+Write owner: setup and the local grant helper both replace the same settings
+file. Each write can succeed atomically; their ordering produces the wrong
+final artifact. No crash or race is required. The grant's read-back verifies an
+intermediate state, not the final result.
+
+Fix direction: persist the grant after the last settings save, or update only
+the telemetry key without replacing the intervening grant. Verify effective
+settings after all setup writes.
+
+## 2. P2 — Enable returns success after history import is cancelled
+
+Locations: `cmd/entire/cli/setup.go:1433` and `:2130`.
+
+Trigger: cancel the parent context during first-time history import. Both
+setup paths call `maybeOfferSessionImport`, then return nil and print `Ready.`
+without checking the cancelled context. The import runner already recognizes
+`context.Canceled` and stops importing, but its void return loses the failure
+at the setup boundary.
+
+The isolated reproduction cancels the context at the import execution seam:
+`ctx.Err()` is `context canceled`, the setup error is nil, and stdout contains
+`Ready.`. This proves orchestration behavior; it is not a subprocess Ctrl-C
+test. Source tracing through `cmd/entire/main.go:148` shows that signal
+termination is only restored when an error is returned, so the nil result also
+bypasses that exit handling.
+
+Setup files and any completed imports remain durable after interruption.
+The existing standalone `entire import <agent>` command owns recovery of the
+unfinished import; reporting successful completion obscures that distinction.
+
+Fix direction: propagate parent cancellation after the import offer in both
+setup paths, while retaining best-effort handling for ordinary import errors.
+
+## 3. P2 — A session cannot be adopted a second time with its original transcript path
+
+Location: `cmd/entire/cli/session_adopt.go:268`.
+
+Trigger: start a Claude session in repo A, adopt it into B, then adopt it from
+B into C. A → B succeeds. Adoption deliberately preserves A's live transcript
+path (`session_adopt.go:455`), while changing the state’s worktree to B. The
+next adoption validates the preserved path against Claude's session directory
+for B, and rejects it as an unexpected transcript path. `--force` cannot
+bypass this validation.
+
+The reproduction uses three isolated repositories and the real Claude path
+resolver. The first `runAdopt` succeeds; the second returns `unexpected
+transcript path ... is not owned by a registered agent`. No transcript content
+is needed or read: the failure occurs in directory ownership validation before
+transcript I/O. The second operation rejects before mutation, leaving the
+session in B; this is a blocked workflow, not demonstrated data corruption.
+
+The existing adoption fixture overrides Claude's session directory to the same
+path for every repository, masking the real per-repository directory mismatch.
+
+Fix direction: retain and validate original transcript provenance independently
+of the current tracking worktree, without weakening transcript confinement.
+
+## Verification and discarded leads
+
+Reproductions use a Go overlay in `/tmp/entire-bug-audit-20260913/` so production
+source and repository tests remain unchanged. They use temporary Git repositories
+and the package's isolated auth/config test setup. No real agent E2E was run.
+
+Two initially failing probes were excluded: interactive setup can copy merged
+settings and overwrite an unparseable existing file when called directly, but
+normal command routing sends repositories with existing settings through a
+different path. Those direct-helper failures do not establish ordinary CLI
+bugs. The prior backlog's external-agent scope-write issue is already fixed in
+the named grant helper.
+
+No fixes, commits, or remote updates were made during this audit. The existing
+`BUG_FIX_CANDIDATES.md` was left untouched.
*** End Patch"));

+## 1. P2 — Unicode branch names corrupt generated trail titles
+
+Source: `cmd/entire/cli/trail/trail.go:197`, called from
+`cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:1089`.
+
+`entire trail create --branch feature/éclair`, with no explicit title, derives
+the title through `HumanizeBranchName`. It uppercases `name[:1]`, which is one
+byte rather than one character. Splitting the UTF-8 encoding of `é` creates
+invalid UTF-8. Normal validation accepts it, and JSON serialization replaces
+the broken bytes: the request title is `��clair`.
+
+Verified through field resolution, normal validation, and serialization of the
+actual create-request type. No remote request was made. An explicit `--title`
+avoids this path. Fix direction: uppercase the first decoded rune and preserve
+the remaining bytes.
+
+## 2. P2 — A non-ASCII title can make automatic trail creation fail
+
+Source: `cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:2396`; resulting error at `:1105`.
+
+On `main`, `entire trail create --title '修复登录' --base main` fails with
+`branch name is required`. Automatic branch derivation drops everything except
+ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and slashes, turning the supplied title into an
+empty branch. The user supplied a valid title, and Git accepts a branch named
+`修复登录`.

+Confirmed through `newTrailCreateCmd().Execute()` in an isolated Git repository,
+with a separate successful `ValidateBranchName("修复登录")` control. Supplying
+`--branch` avoids the failure. Fix direction: preserve valid Unicode letters in
+the slug, or provide a usable fallback and an actionable branch-selection error
+when conversion produces nothing.

+matching `^TestAuditUnicode`. Those tests pass while asserting the observed bugs.

+
+Source: `cmd/entire/cli/trail_review_cmd.go:1304`. The finding-create request
+also trims the patch at `:813`.
+
+`combinedSafeUnifiedDiffPatch` calls `strings.TrimSpace` on the entire unified
+diff. If the final added line ends in spaces or a tab, those bytes belong to the
+suggested file content. Trimming them changes the edit before Git sees it.

+before the newline). Raw `runGitApply` preserves both spaces. Applying the same
+patch through `applyTrailReviewSuggestions` succeeds and reports one applied
+suggestion, but writes `after\n`. The outer `trail finding apply` command calls
+this function after verifying HEAD; that check does not prevent the corruption.
+The create path can already remove the bytes before posting the suggestion.

+the expected-content assertion fails only through trail suggestion handling.

+with a trimmed copy. Preserve patch bytes on both create and apply paths.

+`patch_repro_test.go`, and `patch-results.txt`.
